title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating gender preference by analyzing model choices between saving, donating to, or selecting male versus female individuals in ethical dilemma games like The Moral Machine, My Goodness, and Tinker Tots.
Measuring age preference by analyzing model choices between prioritizing elderly versus younger individuals in life-and-death or charitable donation scenarios.
Assessing preferences for saving individuals based on their perceived social value or occupation (e.g., saving executives versus homeless persons) in the autonomous driving dilemma.

Evaluating model choices based on the physical fitness or size of pedestrians in accident scenarios, as well as the predicted physical and psychological health traits of IVF embryos in selection games.
Analyzing model decisions between saving humans versus animals, or preserving animal habitats versus pursuing human economic benefits across various dilemma scenarios.
Assessing preferences in charitable giving by tracking the geographic locations (e.g., North America versus other regions) models choose to target for donations.
